# Incident Report: NetSupport RAT Infection via Fake Software/Crack Site

**Evidence source:** `2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (26,922 packets, 2024-11-26 08:49:38–09:43:58 UTC, 54 min) plus Suricata alert export `2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise-alerts.txt`.

## Victim host

| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.11.26.183 | Source of all malicious traffic; consistent across alerts and pcap |
| MAC | d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b | ARP: `arp.src.proto_ipv4==10.11.26.183` bound to this MAC; matches `eth.src` on all frames sourced from .183 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-B8TQK49 (NetBIOS workgroup/site name NEMOTODES; AD domain **nemotoads.health**, DC = NEMOTODE-DC / 10.11.26.3) | NBNS name table broadcast from 10.11.26.183; DNS SRV/LDAP lookups for `nemotoads.health` and `NEMOTODES-DC.nemotoads.health` |
| Logged-in user | **oboomwald** | Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS traffic between 10.11.26.183 and DC 10.11.26.3 |

The LAN gateway is 10.11.26.1 (MAC 00:17:e0:b8:29:5e) and the domain controller is 10.11.26.3 (MAC 00:24:e8:7f:09:5d) — both confirmed distinct from the victim.

## Malware family and attribution

**NetSupport RAT** (the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-control client, `client32.exe`, abused as a commodity RAT) — delivered through a **ZPHP-style fake software/crack download** loader.

**Attribution: signature-confirmed**, corroborated by direct protocol observation:
- Suricata alerts: `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`, `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`, `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin`/`Response`, `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request`, and `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in DNS Lookup/TLS SNI (modandcrackedapk.com)`.
- I independently verified the C2 protocol by extracting the HTTP objects from stream 77/140: request/response bodies contain the literal NetSupport client32 command grammar `CMD=POLL / INFO=1 / ACK=1` and `CMD=ENCD / ES=1 / DATA=<binary>`, which is the documented NetSupport Manager wire protocol, not a generic HTTP beacon.

## Timeline / delivery chain

1. **08:50:10 UTC (t+32.8s)** — Host queries `classicgrand.com` → 213.246.109.5 (TLS), 3.5 MB exchanged — redirect/loader stage.
2. **08:50:13 UTC (t+35.7s)** — Host queries `modandcrackedapk.com` → 193.42.38.139 (TLS SNI, flagged by ET as a ZPHP domain) and `confirmsubscription.com` → 52.8.34.0 / 13.56.30.207 almost simultaneously — fake CAPTCHA/subscription-confirmation redirect stage.
3. **08:50:13–08:50:50 UTC** — 10 MB downloaded from 193.42.38.139 over TLS (encrypted; payload content not recoverable from this capture, but the volume and timing are consistent with the RAT installer).
4. **08:50:45 UTC (t+62s)** — Final request to `modandcrackedapk.com`, followed by a Let's Encrypt OCSP check (`r10.o.lencr.org`).
5. **08:50:45 UTC (t+67.2s)** — Host queries `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` → 104.26.1.231 and GETs `/location/loca.asp`, receiving geo-coordinates `33.7488,-84.3877` (Atlanta, GA) — this is the NetSupport client's own startup geolocation check.
6. **08:50:45 UTC (t+67.4s)** — First C2 POST to `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` on port 443 (plaintext HTTP, not TLS). Beaconing continues every ~60 seconds for the remainder of the capture (last POST at t+3231s / 08:44:29 UTC), 65+ checkins total.

## Indicators of Compromise

| Type | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| c2_endpoint | **194.180.191.64:443** | 65+ HTTP POST requests to `/fakeurl.htm` containing `CMD=POLL`/`CMD=ENCD` NetSupport client32 protocol strings; ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity / Malicious NetSupport RAT CnC Checkin alerts |
| url | **http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm** | Exported HTTP object; request/response bodies recovered |
| domain | **modandcrackedapk.com** (→ 193.42.38.139) | DNS A-record answers at t+35.7s/37.3s/62.1s; TLS SNI; ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain alerts (DNS + TLS SNI); 10 MB encrypted transfer immediately preceding RAT startup |
| domain | **classicgrand.com** (→ 213.246.109.5) | DNS A-record answer at t+32.8s; TLS SNI; first hop in the redirect chain, 3.5 MB exchanged |
| domain | **confirmsubscription.com** (→ 52.8.34.0, 13.56.30.207) | DNS A-record answers at t+35.7s/37.3s, concurrent with modandcrackedapk.com lookups — part of the same redirect chain |
| domain | geo.netsupportsoftware.com (→ 104.26.1.231) | DNS query + HTTP GET `/location/loca.asp` at t+67.2s, seconds before first C2 checkin; ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request alert |
| url | http://geo.netsupportsoftware.com/location/loca.asp | Exported HTTP object, response `33.7488,-84.3877` |

**No file name or SHA256 could be grounded.** The actual payload transfer to 193.42.38.139 occurred entirely over TLS; the capture contains no decryption keys, so the installer/dropper content is not recoverable from this evidence. Do not report a hash for this incident — none was observed.

## Benign context (not indicators)

- Microsoft telemetry/services: `login.live.com`, `office.com`/`officeapps.live.com`, `msn.com`/`bing.com`, `smartscreen.microsoft.com`, `windowsupdate.com` (CTL/cert downloads), `client.wns.windows.com`.
- `acroipm2.adobe.com`, `armmf.adobe.com` and the exported `ProcessMAU.txt` — Adobe ARM update-check telemetry.
- Google/CDN assets (`fonts.googleapis.com`, `www.google.com`, `maps.googleapis.com`, `code.jquery.com`) — loaded as decoration by the lure page.
- `r10.o.lencr.org` — routine Let's Encrypt OCSP revocation check.
- Domain-joined LAN chatter to 10.11.26.3 (LDAP, Kerberos, CLDAP, DCERPC/drsuapi/samr, NBNS, SMBv1/NTLMSSP, mailslot browser announcements) and local WPAD/mDNS/SSDP/LLMNR broadcast noise — normal AD workstation behavior, not attacker activity. (Note: the SMBv1/NTLMSSP overflow-pattern alerts against the DC are standard Windows domain SMB negotiation traffic tripping generic-signature IDS rules, not an observed exploitation attempt in the packet contents.)

## Summary

User **oboomwald** on Windows workstation **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** (10.11.26.183, MAC d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b), domain-joined to **nemotoads.health**, was redirected through `classicgrand.com` → `confirmsubscription.com` to a fake software/crack download site `modandcrackedapk.com` (193.42.38.139), which delivered a **NetSupport RAT** payload over an encrypted 10 MB TLS transfer. Within seconds of the download, the client performed its startup geolocation check against `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` and began persistent HTTP POST beaconing to **194.180.191.64:443** using the NetSupport client32 CMD=POLL/CMD=ENCD protocol, continuing for the remainder of the ~54-minute capture.
